title: "How Social Media Influencers Build Brand Loyalty Among Millennial Consumers"

# --- Mode: manuscript (the main document) or article (a publication-style
#     preview for sharing drafts; PDF and .tex only) ---
ama-mode: manuscript

# --- Abstract (at most 200 words, in the third person) ---
abstract: |
  Social media has changed the way brands connect with consumers. With the
  rise of social media influencers, many brands use them to reach and
  engage their target audiences. This research investigates the role of
  social media influencers in building brand loyalty among millennial
  consumers. The authors use a mixed-methods approach that combines an
  online survey with in-depth interviews. The findings suggest that
  influencers strengthen brand loyalty, and that this effect is larger for
  familiar brands. The research offers guidance on how brands can work with
  influencers to connect with their target audiences.

Social media has become an essential part of daily life, and it has changed
the way consumers communicate with one another. It has also changed the way
brands connect with consumers. Many brands now work with social media
influencers to reach and engage their target audiences. Influencers have a
large following on social media platforms and are viewed as experts in a
particular niche. Followers see them as trusted sources of information, and
influencers can shape their followers' purchase decisions.

# Theoretical Background

Brand loyalty represents the degree to which customers are committed to
purchasing a particular brand. Loyalty matters because it leads to repeat
purchases and positive word of mouth, which in turn increase sales and
profitability.[^fn1] Language also shapes how consumers respond to
recommendations [@lafreniere2022; @ozturan2022].

[^fn1]: Use footnotes sparingly (most articles have no more than 10), and
keep each footnote to 40 words or fewer.

## Social Media Influencers and Brand Loyalty

Influencers can strengthen brand loyalty by providing valuable content and
by engaging with their followers. This research focuses on millennial
consumers because they are the most active users of social media.

::: {.hypothesis}
H~1~: Trust in an influencer increases loyalty to the brands that the
influencer endorses.
:::

::: {.hypothesis}
H~2~: The effect of trust in an influencer on brand loyalty is stronger for
familiar brands than for unfamiliar brands.
:::

## Millennial Consumers

Millennial consumers are an important target audience because they are the
largest generation in the workforce and have substantial buying power.
Research in marketing has examined how scholarship in the field develops
and is evaluated [@gupta2023; @sridhar2023].

# Study 1

## Method

### Participants and design

Two hundred members of an online panel (51.0% female, 47.5% male, 1.0%
nonbinary, .5% preferred not to state) completed the survey. Participants
rated their trust in an influencer they follow, their familiarity with a
brand the influencer endorses, and their loyalty to that brand.

### Measures

All measures used seven-point scales. @tbl-descriptives reports descriptive
statistics.

| Variable         | M    | SD   | n   |
|:-----------------|-----:|-----:|----:|
| Brand loyalty^a^ | 4.21 | 1.02 | 200 |
| Purchase intent  | 3.87 | 1.15 | 200 |
| Influencer trust | 4.56 |  .89 | 200 |

: Loyalty and Trust Are Above the Scale Midpoint {#tbl-descriptives}

::: {.notes}
^a^Average of four items.

All variables were measured on seven-point scales.
:::

## Results

Equation 1 presents the model:

$$
\text{Loyalty}_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Trust}_i + \beta_2 \text{Familiarity}_i + \beta_3 \text{Trust}_i \times \text{Familiarity}_i + \varepsilon_i.
$$ {#eq-model}

Trust in the influencer was positively associated with brand loyalty
(b = .38, SE = .08, *p* < .001), and this association was stronger for
familiar brands (b = .15, SE = .06, *p* = .013; @tbl-regression and
@fig-loyalty).

| Predictor              | Model 1    | Model 2    |
|:-----------------------|:----------:|:----------:|
| Intercept              | 2.45 (.21) | 2.31 (.20) |
| Influencer trust       |  .42 (.08) |  .38 (.08) |
| Brand familiarity      |  .28 (.07) |  .25 (.07) |
| Trust × Familiarity    |            |  .15 (.06) |
| R^2^                   |  .31       |  .34       |

: Influencer Trust Predicts Brand Loyalty {#tbl-regression}

::: {.notes}
Unstandardized coefficients, with standard errors in parentheses. The text
reports the *p*-values.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-loyalty
#| fig-cap: "Influencer Trust Increases Loyalty More for Familiar Brands"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.6

library(ggplot2)

# Estimated means and standard errors from Model 2
loyalty <- data.frame(
  trust = factor(rep(c("Low Trust", "High Trust"), times = 2),
                 levels = c("Low Trust", "High Trust")),
  familiarity = rep(c("Unfamiliar brand", "Familiar brand"), each = 2),
  mean = c(3.62, 4.05, 3.80, 4.88),
  se = c(.14, .13, .14, .12)
)

# AMA: Arial in figures, both axes labeled, error bars, the full scale range
ggplot(loyalty, aes(x = trust, y = mean, fill = familiarity)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = .7), width = .6, color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
                position = position_dodge(width = .7), width = .15) +
  geom_text(aes(y = mean + se, label = sprintf("%.2f", mean)),
            position = position_dodge(width = .7), vjust = -.6, size = 3.5,
            family = "sans") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey35", "grey80")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 7), breaks = 1:7, oob = scales::oob_keep) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 7)) +
  labs(x = "Trust in the Influencer", y = "Brand Loyalty", fill = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

::: {.notes}
Error bars represent ±1 SE.
:::

# General Discussion

The findings indicate that influencers can strengthen brand loyalty among
millennial consumers and that familiar brands benefit the most. The Web
Appendix reports the stimuli (Web Appendix A) and robustness checks (Web
Appendix B).
